trials.output_text: {"subjective": "The patient reports headaches almost every evening for three weeks. The headaches are described as heavy and pressing at the back of the head and sometimes across the forehead. They are not sharp. Paracetamol helps a little. The headaches worsen with stress at work and skipping lunch. The patient experiences occasional blurry vision in the evening, but it clears. There is no vomiting or weakness. The patient reports waking up two times per night to urinate and experiencing increased thirst. The patient has lost about 2-3 kilograms without intending to. The patient reports tingling in both feet, mostly at night, which is getting worse. The patient has been taking amlodipine five milligrams once daily for blood pressure, but misses it sometimes. The patient takes metformin five hundred milligrams twice daily with meals (morning dose only). The patient checks home blood pressure occasionally and reports readings of 150/94 and 148/92. The patient has a glucometer and morning blood sugar is around 9-10, after meal it is around 12. The patient reports feeling tired on the stairs. The patient eats tea with two spoons of sugar and bread in the morning, rice or ugali with stew for lunch, fried fish for dinner, and drinks soda almost every day (one to two half litre sodas). The patient adds a lot of salt to their food. The patient stopped smoking four years ago and drinks 2-3 beers on Saturdays. The patient does not exercise regularly, only walking to the stage in the morning (10 minutes). The patient has a family history of diabetes, stroke, and high blood pressure. The patient reports no allergies. The patient is worried about their health and work. They sleep poorly, maybe five hours per night. The patient experiences mood changes but not feeling very low. The patient uses ibuprofen three times a week for headaches.", "objective": "Blood pressure: 150/94 (first reading), 148/92 (second reading). Pulse: 78 bpm, regular. Weight: 82 kg (3 kg less than last time). Temperature: Normal. Heart sounds: Normal. Chest: Clear. Abdomen: Soft, no tenderness. Ankle swelling: Mild pitting at both ankles. Foot exam: Reduced sensation on the soles of both feet and reduced ankle reflexes. Random blood sugar: 11.2 mmol/L. The patient is wearing closed shoes.", "assessment": "The patient presents with headaches likely related to uncontrolled hypertension and possibly exacerbated by stress, poor sleep, and lifestyle factors (high sodium intake, excessive soda consumption). There are signs of poorly controlled diabetes, including elevated blood glucose levels, increased thirst, and nighttime urination. Peripheral neuropathy is suspected due to the tingling in the feet. The patient's blood pressure and blood sugar are above target. The patient has a family history of stroke and diabetes.", "plan": "Increase amlodipine to 10 mg once daily, taken at the same time every morning. Increase metformin to 1 gram with breakfast and 500 mg with dinner, taken with food. Stop ibuprofen due to potential kidney strain and blood pressure elevation. Monitor home blood pressure and morning blood sugar for two weeks and bring results to follow-up appointment. Perform glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP) including creatinine and electrolytes, lipid profile, and urine protein test. Order an ECG today. Refer patient to the eye clinic. Advise patient to cut soda completely and reduce sugar in tea. Reduce salt intake and choose grilled fish over fried. Encourage 30 minutes of walking at least five days a week. Limit beer consumption to one on Saturdays. Instruct patient to check feet daily for any wounds or blisters, wear closed shoes, and bring any concerns to the clinic immediately. Keep headache diary. Schedule follow-up appointment in two weeks, sooner if severe headaches, vomiting, vision loss, chest pain, weakness, or confusion occur. Wife should accompany patient to appointments."}
